verdict: PSEG's regulated utility earned a steady $506 million, but mark-to-market losses at its power business cut total GAAP profit to $376 million, down from $622 million a year ago.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Down from $1.24 a year ago; non-GAAP operating EPS was $1.15

kpis.label: Utility (PSE&G) profit
kpis.note: Steady regulated earnings, vs $515M a year ago

segments.name: PSE&G (regulated utility)
segments.note: New Jersey's largest electric and gas utility — delivering power and gas to about 2.4 million electric and 1.9 million gas customers at regulated prices.

segments.name: PSEG Power & Other
segments.note: Nuclear power generation and other businesses, shown net of $38M of intersegment eliminations (gross revenue $532M, down from $749M as market-linked sales fell).

opex.name: Operation & maintenance
opex.note: Running the grid and the nuclear plants, including storm restoration after severe summer weather.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of grids and power plants over their long lives — a non-cash charge.

otherDetail: A net $243M drag: $280M of interest expense and a $28M loss on nuclear decommissioning trust investments, partly offset by $44M of other income and a $21M pension credit.
footerNote: Adaptation for a utility: energy costs — fuel and purchased power — are treated as the cost of revenue; the remaining lines mirror PSEG's consolidating income statement. Segment revenue for Power & Other is net of intersegment eliminations so the segments add to total revenue.
oneTimers: Mark-to-market accounting losses of $251M before tax and a $21M loss on nuclear decommissioning trust investments hit GAAP results. Excluding reconciling items of $198M after tax, non-GAAP operating earnings were $574M ($1.15 per share).

takeaways.title: The utility is the steady core
takeaways.text: PSE&G earned $506M, nearly matching last year's $515M, as infrastructure investment and customer growth offset higher depreciation and interest costs.

takeaways.title: Power swung to a loss
takeaways.text: PSEG Power & Other lost $130M (vs a $107M profit a year ago) on mark-to-market and trust-investment losses — the entire reason group profit fell.

takeaways.title: Nuclear plants ran hard
takeaways.text: PSEG's nuclear fleet produced 8.2 terawatt-hours of carbon-free power at a 95.5% capacity factor — running almost flat-out through the summer storm season.
